title: Smooth fibres have regular local rings
statement: Let $\varphi:R\to S$ be a smooth ring map [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map]. For every prime ideal $\mathfrak p\subset R$, the base-change map $\kappa(\mathfrak p)\to S\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is smooth, and for every prime $\mathfrak Q$ of the fibre the localization $(S\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p))_{\mathfrak Q}$ is a regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme]. The residue field and fibre are understood as in [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime].

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00T4 (lemma-base-change-smooth, line 37133), and Lemma Tag 00TT (lemma-characterize-smooth-over-field, line 38609), whose final assertion gives regularity of the local ring

proof.text: Fix a prime ideal $\mathfrak p\subset R$ and put $k=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ and $A=S\otimes_Rk$. Applying the base-change clause of [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-base-change-composition] to the smooth map $R\to S$ and the residue-field map $R\to k$ shows that $k\to A$ is smooth.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00T4 (lemma-base-change-smooth, line 37133), with R' = kappa(p)

proof.text: For every prime ideal $\mathfrak Q\subset A$, [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-over-field-regular-local] applied to the smooth $k$-algebra $A$ from Step 1 gives that $A_{\mathfrak Q}=(S\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p))_{\mathfrak Q}$ is a regular local ring. Since $\mathfrak p$ and $\mathfrak Q$ were arbitrary, this proves both assertions.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00TT (lemma-characterize-smooth-over-field, line 38609), final assertion
